newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin sacked aide over Belarus - Tass.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin sacked aide over Belarus - Tass.

text.p: Boris Yeltsin sacked his top foreign policy aide over his handling of a Union Treaty signed with Belarus last week, Itar-Tass news agency said on Saturday.
On Friday the Kremlin said Yeltsin had relieved Dmitry Ryurikov of his duties after nearly six years coordinating foreign policy in the presidential administration.
"(Yeltsin) was extremely dissastisfied with the level of documents offered for signature by the Presidents of Russia and Belarus on April 2," Tass quoted a Kremlin source as saying.

"Dmitry Ryurikov was one of those in the president's administration who was directly responsible for the preparation of the documents linked with Russian-Belarussian integration," it said, quoting the source.
Yeltsin signed a largely symbolic Union Treaty with Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko on Wednesday after last-minute changes dramatically scaling back the deal.

On Saturday he told Russians not to worry that integration was happening behind their backs or that they would be dragged down by Russia's western neighbour, whose hardline president has stalled market reforms and cracked down on freedom of speech.

"I will not hide that some politicians thought it would be possible, having signed the Treaty and memorandum, to present our peoples with a fait accompli. That is wrong. Russians should all get the chance to have their say in the making of such an important decision," Yeltsin said.
Russian Public Television said on Friday that Kremlin spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky, 42, would coordinate foreign policy in the presidential administration from now on.

The moustachioed Ryurikov, 50, kept a low public profile but played a key behind-the-scenes role planning negotiations over NATO expansion plans, arms control and other controversial post-Cold War issues and preparing summit meetings.
